assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defines incretin physiology and converted it into a therapeutic class: GLP-1 biology, proglucagon-derived peptide structure and action, and long-acting agonists that now transform treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. Originality, clarity and very large, continuing clinical and societal impact all score highly.
assessment.attribution: Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form and early synthesis), Holst (physiology of the gut hormone in humans) and Drucker (GLP-1 receptor biology, GLP-2, translation) form a coherent trio. Knudsen's drug-development role (liraglutide, semaglutide) is real but industrial; the Habener contribution is not in the credited names and credit among peptide discoverers is contested, so I cannot resolve it from this list alone.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple large randomized outcome trials, regulatory approvals and a decade of real-world use confirm efficacy and the underlying physiology. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Mojsov, Habener, Holst, Drucker and the industrial developers is disputed and limited to three names here.
Long-term safety and durability of obesity treatment are still accumulating, though this does not weaken the mechanistic discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering T cells with chimeric antigen receptors created a new modality of living drug that produces durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies. Conceptually original, clinically decisive and a founding example of cell therapy.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (second-generation costimulatory CARs, preclinical proof), June (clinical translation to CLL and ALL) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified lymphocyte trials) are plausible. Eshhar and others who made first-generation chimeric receptors are not in the credited names, which leaves a fairness question; I lean on my own recollection of the field history rather than verified sources.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation across several approved products and thousands of patients; long-term remissions now documented. Timely, though toxicity and solid-tumour limits remain.
uncertainties: Priority of first-generation chimeric receptor work versus later costimulation-based designs is not resolved by the supplied credit.
Rosenberg's contribution is broader adoptive therapy (TIL), and the committee may regard it as a distinct discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle vaccines against HPV provide near-complete protection from persistent infection and precancerous lesions, and population data show falling cervical disease. A rare case of a vaccine that prevents cancer, with clear mechanism and enormous public-health impact.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity) and Frazer (early VLP work and the Gardasil/Cervarix-enabling technology) are a defensible trio, although Zhou, Frazer and others are linked to the early expression work and priority among VLP groups is debated. The Nobel was already given in 2008 for HPV causing cervical cancer, which is a distinct discovery.
assessment.maturity: Mature: long-term efficacy, herd-protection and cancer-incidence reduction data from several countries. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority dispute among VLP developers (including Jian Zhou, who is not credited) is not resolved.
Whether the committee treats vaccine development as sufficiently distinct from the 2008 HPV prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense oligonucleotide correction of SMN2 exon 7 splicing led to nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, converting a lethal infantile disease into a treatable one. Strong mechanistic clarity from splicing biology to bedside, and a template for RNA therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and identification of the ISS-N1 target strategy) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and clinical development at Ionis) are a natural pair; Hua, Singh and others contributed to target identification and are not credited. The pair is plausible but not obviously complete.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with durable clinical benefit and extensive follow-up; independent confirmation through trials and later SMN-directed therapies. Timing is appropriate and perhaps early relative to other candidates.
uncertainties: Whether the pair fairly represents the discovery, or whether early ASO chemistry should be recognized separately.
Relative weight of therapy development versus basic discovery of the SMN2 splicing switch.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis (Solexa/Illumina) drove a thousand-fold fall in sequencing cost and underlies modern genomics, cancer genomics, diagnostics and pathogen surveillance. Technology-enabled impact is immense and broadly across biology and medicine.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived the single-molecule array and reversible-terminator approach; Mayer (clustered colony amplification, Manteia) is credited here. Other companies and inventors (e.g. Church, Shendure, 454, Lynx) contributed to the broader field, so a prize on sequencing has contested credit boundaries.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and ubiquitous, with a clear record of use. Recognition is arguably late; methods precedent exists with PCR and sequencing in earlier prizes (Sanger was a chemistry laureate).
uncertainties: Whether a technology prize in this area is better placed in chemistry than physiology or medicine.
Priority and credit versus other parallel-sequencing inventors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational inhibition of BCR-ABL with imatinib produced a paradigm of targeted cancer therapy, turning chronic myeloid leukaemia from fatal to a chronic manageable disease. Clear, original and highly consequential.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound development), Druker (clinical trials and advocacy) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) is a sound trio. Basic discovery of BCR-ABL (Rowley, Gallo, Baltimore, Witte) is not credited and may be considered foundational.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with 20+ years of survival data. Recognition is timely to late; the idea has already been widely rewarded through Lasker prizes.
uncertainties: Fair recognition of upstream BCR-ABL and kinase biology versus drug development.
Whether the committee sees this as a clinical-translational prize it wishes to make.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Human genetic discovery that PCSK9 variants control LDL cholesterol, followed by therapeutic inhibitors that reduce cardiovascular events. A model of human genetics validating a drug target, with a clear mechanistic chain.
assessment.attribution: Seidah (identification and biochemistry of PCSK9), Hobbs and Cohen (loss-of-function variants and cardiovascular protection in Dallas Heart Study) are a natural group; Abifadel and Boileau (first gain-of-function families) have a strong claim to the discovery that PCSK9 causes hypercholesterolaemia, which complicates a three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by outcome trials and approved drugs. Timing is reasonable though the Goldstein and Brown 1985 prize on LDL receptors partly overlaps.
uncertainties: Credit for the original gain-of-function discovery (Abifadel, Boileau) versus protective variants.
Overlap with prior LDL receptor prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Channelrhodopsin and related microbial opsins give millisecond control of genetically defined cells with light, transforming causal neuroscience across circuits and behaviour. Methodologically original with wide uptake, though direct clinical impact is limited so far.
assessment.attribution: Nagel, Bamberg and Hegemann identified and characterised channelrhodopsin; Boyden and Deisseroth established neuronal use; Miesenboeck made an earlier light-gated approach. Six credited names exceed three places, so any selection is contentious. The trio chosen balances discovery and neuronal application.
assessment.maturity: Methodologically mature and replicated across thousands of labs; clinical optogenetics (vision restoration) is early. Timely on method grounds.
uncertainties: Three-laureate limit excludes Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck, each with substantive claims.
Priority disputes between Boyden and Deisseroth teams; technology-versus-discovery weighting.
